cats.d: Hot, fast and charred. Preheat until the display says Add Food.
Low and slow with real wood pellets. ½ cup is enough.
Crispy wings, fries and snacks with a hint of smoke.
Grilled fruit, s'mores and campfire treats.

recipes.title: Smoky garlic butter steak
recipes.blurb: Charred outside, juicy inside, with a whisper of hardwood smoke.
ing: 2 ribeye or strip steaks, 1 inch thick
2 tbsp butter mixed with 1 grated garlic clove and parsley
steps: Take steaks out 30 minutes early. Oil and season well.
Fill the smoke box with pellets and press Woodfire Flavor. Select Grill, HI, and preheat.
Grill 4–5 minutes per side for medium-rare (130°F on a thermometer).
Rest 5 minutes topped with the garlic butter.
notes: USDA safe minimum for steak is 145°F plus a 3-minute rest. Many people prefer 130–135°F; your call.
recipes.healthier: Choose a leaner sirloin, trim the fat, use half the butter and fill half the plate with grilled veg.

recipes.title: Classic backyard burgers
recipes.blurb: Juicy smash-style burgers with smoky edges.
steps: Form 4 patties slightly wider than the buns. Press a dimple in the centre.
Fill the smoke box with pellets and press Woodfire Flavor. Grill on HI and preheat.
Grill 4–5 minutes per side to 160°F. Add cheese for the last minute.
Toast buns on the grate 30 seconds.
recipes.healthier: Use 90/10 beef or ground turkey and wrap in lettuce instead of a bun.

recipes.title: Honey lime chicken thighs
recipes.blurb: Sticky, sweet and a little charred. Kids' favourite.
steps: Mix honey, lime, soy and garlic. Marinate the chicken 30 minutes (or overnight).
Fill the smoke box with pellets and press Woodfire Flavor. Grill on MED and preheat.
Grill 6–7 minutes per side until 165°F inside.
Brush with leftover marinade only in the first half of cooking.
recipes.healthier: Use skinless chicken breast and halve the honey; the lime and smoke carry the flavor.

recipes.title: Shrimp & veggie skewers
recipes.blurb: Fast weeknight skewers. Lemon, garlic and smoke.
ing: 1 zucchini and 1 bell pepper, in chunks
steps: Toss everything with oil, garlic, lemon and spices. Thread onto skewers.
Fill the smoke box with pellets and press Woodfire Flavor. Grill on HI and preheat.
Grill 2–3 minutes per side until shrimp are pink and opaque.
Squeeze more lemon on top.
recipes.healthier: Already light. Use 1 tbsp oil instead of 3.

recipes.title: Smoked pulled pork
recipes.blurb: The weekend project. Fall-apart tender with real bark.
ing: Buns, slaw and BBQ sauce to serve
steps: Rub the pork all over. Rest 1 hour or overnight in the fridge.
Fill the smoke box with pellets. Select Smoker at 250°F and preheat.
Smoke until the internal temperature reaches 200–203°F, about 8–10 hours. Wrap in foil at 165°F if the bark looks dark enough.
Rest 30 minutes wrapped, then shred with forks.
notes: Top up pellets only if the smoke stops in the first few hours; after that the bark is set.
recipes.healthier: Trim the fat cap before smoking, serve sauce on the side and pile it on slaw instead of a bun.

recipes.title: Smoked baby back ribs
recipes.blurb: Tender ribs with a sticky glaze, no fuss.
steps: Pull the membrane off the back of the ribs. Season with rub.
Fill the smoke box. Smoker at 250°F, preheat.
Smoke 3 hours, wrap in foil with a splash of apple juice for 1½ hours.
Unwrap, brush with sauce mixed with honey, smoke 30 more minutes until tacky.
recipes.healthier: Brush the glaze on only for the last 10 minutes and serve with a big salad.

recipes.title: Smoked salmon fillet
recipes.blurb: Flaky, smoky and done in under an hour.
steps: Mix sugar, salt and pepper. Rub on the salmon flesh and rest 30 minutes in the fridge. Pat dry.
Fill the smoke box. Smoker at 250°F, preheat.
Smoke skin-side down 45–60 minutes until 145°F.
Serve with lemon and dill.
recipes.healthier: Already a great pick. Use half the sugar in the cure.

recipes.title: Smoked mac & cheese
recipes.blurb: Creamy mac that picks up smoke on top. Party side.
ing: 1 lb elbow pasta, cooked al dente
steps: Mix pasta with milk, cream, butter, 2 cups cheese and seasoning in a foil pan.
Top with the rest of the cheese.
Fill the smoke box. Smoker at 250°F. Smoke uncovered 1 hour, stirring once.
recipes.healthier: Use half the cheese and stir in steamed broccoli or cauliflower.

recipes.title: Smoky crispy wings
recipes.blurb: Air-crisped wings with a smoke kiss. No deep fryer.
ing: 2 lbs chicken wings, patted very dry
steps: Toss wings with baking powder, salt and paprika.
Fill the smoke box, select Air Crisp at 390°F with the crisper basket, preheat.
Cook 25–30 minutes, shaking halfway, until 165°F and crispy.
Toss in sauce.
recipes.healthier: Use plain smoked paprika wings with hot sauce instead of a sugary BBQ glaze.

recipes.title: Woodfire fries
recipes.blurb: Hand-cut fries with a smoky edge.
steps: Soak fries in cold water 30 minutes. Dry very well.
Toss with oil.
Air Crisp at 390°F in the basket 20–25 minutes, shaking twice. Salt straight away.
recipes.healthier: Use sweet potatoes and just 1 tsp oil; they crisp up fine.

recipes.title: Crispy smashed potatoes
recipes.blurb: Boiled baby potatoes, smashed and crisped.
steps: Boil potatoes 15 minutes until tender. Drain and smash flat with a glass.
Brush with garlic oil, season.
Air Crisp at 390°F for 15–18 minutes. Sprinkle Parmesan.
recipes.healthier: Use 1 tbsp oil and skip the Parmesan, or use a light dusting.

recipes.title: Sausage & pepper hoagies
recipes.blurb: Juicy sausages and sweet peppers, crisped in one basket.
steps: Toss peppers and onion with oil.
Fill the smoke box with pellets and press Woodfire Flavor. Air Crisp at 375°F, preheat.
Cook sausages and veg 15–18 minutes, shaking once, until sausages reach 160°F.
Pile into rolls.
recipes.healthier: Use chicken sausages and serve on a whole-wheat roll.

recipes.title: Woodfire margherita pizza
recipes.blurb: Pizza-oven vibes in the backyard.
steps: Stretch dough to fit the grill plate. Top with sauce and mozzarella.
Fill the smoke box with pellets and press Woodfire Flavor. Bake at 450°F, preheat.
Bake 10–12 minutes until the crust is golden.
Finish with basil and oil.
recipes.healthier: Use whole-wheat dough, half the cheese and add peppers and mushrooms.

recipes.title: Garlic herb flatbread
recipes.blurb: Blistered flatbread for dips and grilled meats.
ing: 3 tbsp butter melted with 2 garlic cloves
steps: Stretch dough thin and dimple with fingers. Brush with garlic butter.
Fill the smoke box with pellets and press Woodfire Flavor. Bake at 425°F, preheat.
Bake 8–10 minutes. Brush with more butter and sprinkle parsley and salt.
recipes.healthier: Brush with olive oil and garlic instead of butter.

recipes.title: Skillet cornbread
recipes.blurb: Golden cornbread with a crisp crust and a little smoke.
ing: 1 box cornbread mix + egg and milk as directed
steps: Melt butter in a small cast iron pan in the preheating grill.
Pour in the batter.
Bake at 375°F for 18–22 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean. Drizzle honey.
recipes.healthier: Use a whole-grain mix and skip the honey drizzle.

recipes.title: BBQ chicken quesadillas
recipes.blurb: Leftover smoked chicken? This is where it goes.
steps: Toss chicken with BBQ sauce.
Fill half of each tortilla with chicken, onion and cheese; fold.
Bake at 400°F for 6–8 minutes, flipping once, until crisp and melty.
recipes.healthier: Use whole-wheat tortillas, half the cheese and add grilled peppers.

recipes.title: Charred street corn
recipes.blurb: Elote-style: mayo, cheese, lime and chili.
ing: ¼ cup crumbled cotija or feta
steps: Fill the smoke box with pellets and press Woodfire Flavor. Grill on HI, preheat.
Grill corn 10–12 minutes, turning, until charred in spots.
Brush with mayo, roll in cheese, dust with chili and squeeze lime.
recipes.healthier: Use Greek yogurt instead of mayo and go light on the cheese.

recipes.title: Grilled veggie platter
recipes.blurb: Zucchini, peppers, mushrooms and onions with balsamic.
steps: Toss veg with oil and salt.
Fill the smoke box with pellets and press Woodfire Flavor. Grill on MED, preheat.
Grill in batches 3–5 minutes per side.
Drizzle balsamic and scatter herbs.
recipes.healthier: Already healthy. Nothing to change.

recipes.title: Smoky broccoli
recipes.blurb: Crispy-edged broccoli with lemon and Parmesan.
steps: Toss broccoli with oil and seasoning.
Fill the smoke box with pellets and press Woodfire Flavor. Air Crisp at 390°F, preheat.
Cook 10–12 minutes, shaking once. Finish with lemon and Parmesan.
recipes.healthier: Already light. Skip the Parmesan if you like.

recipes.title: Grilled cabbage steaks
recipes.blurb: Thick cabbage slices turn sweet and charred.
steps: Brush cabbage rounds with butter and season.
Fill the smoke box with pellets and press Woodfire Flavor. Grill on MED, preheat.
Grill 6–8 minutes per side until tender and charred.
recipes.healthier: Use olive oil spray instead of butter.

recipes.title: Grilled honey peaches
recipes.blurb: Caramelised peaches with ice cream. Summer on a plate.
steps: Brush cut sides with butter.
Grill on MED cut-side down 4–5 minutes, flip, drizzle honey and cinnamon, 2 more minutes.
Serve warm with ice cream.
recipes.healthier: Serve with Greek yogurt instead of ice cream and skip the butter.

recipes.title: Pineapple with cinnamon sugar
recipes.blurb: Charred pineapple spears, sweet and tangy.
steps: Toss spears with sugar and cinnamon.
Grill on HI 3 minutes per side until marked.
Finish with lime zest.
recipes.healthier: Skip the sugar; grilling caramelizes the pineapple on its own.

recipes.title: S'mores dip
recipes.blurb: Gooey chocolate and toasted marshmallow for dipping.
steps: Spread chocolate in a small cast iron pan. Cover with marshmallows, cut-side down.
Bake at 400°F for 6–8 minutes until marshmallows are golden.
Dip with graham crackers. Careful, it's hot.
recipes.healthier: Use dark chocolate and serve with strawberries to dip.

recipes.title: Campfire banana boats
recipes.blurb: Bananas stuffed with chocolate and marshmallow, baked in foil.
steps: Slit each banana lengthwise through the peel, not all the way through.
Stuff with chocolate and marshmallows. Wrap in foil.
Bake at 375°F for 8–10 minutes. Eat with a spoon.
recipes.healthier: Use dark chocolate chips and half the marshmallows.

recipes.title: Smoked beef brisket
recipes.blurb: The big one. Dark bark, juicy slices, worth the wait.
ing: 5–6 lb brisket flat, fat trimmed to ¼ inch
steps: Mix salt, pepper and garlic. Coat the brisket all over and rest 1 hour.
Fill the smoke box with pellets. Select Smoker at 250°F and preheat.
Smoke fat side up until the bark is dark and the inside reads 165°F, about 5 hours.
Wrap tightly in butcher paper or foil and keep cooking to 203°F, 2–3 hours more.
Rest wrapped for 1 hour, then slice across the grain.
notes: Slice only what you'll eat. Leftovers stay juicier as a whole piece.
recipes.healthier: Choose the flat, trim the fat cap well and serve with grilled vegetables instead of bread.

recipes.title: Smoked whole chicken
recipes.blurb: Golden skin, smoky meat, Sunday dinner without the oven.
steps: Pat the chicken dry. Rub with oil and seasoning. Put lemon and garlic inside.
Fill the smoke box with pellets. Select Smoker at 250°F and preheat.
Smoke until the thickest part of the thigh reads 165°F, about 3 hours.
Switch to Grill HI for the last 5 minutes to crisp the skin.
Rest 10 minutes before carving.
recipes.healthier: Remove the skin before eating and serve with a big salad.

recipes.title: Smoked turkey breast
recipes.blurb: Holiday flavor any weekend. Great for sandwiches all week.
steps: Brush the turkey with butter and season all over.
Fill the smoke box with pellets. Select Smoker at 250°F and preheat.
Smoke until the center reads 160°F, about 2½ hours.
Tent with foil and rest 15 minutes. It climbs to 165°F.
recipes.healthier: Swap butter for olive oil and use the leftovers for lean lunch wraps.

recipes.title: Smoked queso dip
recipes.blurb: Melty, smoky cheese dip. Party starter, no stovetop.
ing: 1 can diced tomatoes with green chiles
½ lb cooked ground beef or chorizo
steps: Put everything except the chips in a foil pan.
Fill the smoke box with pellets. Select Smoker at 250°F and preheat.
Smoke 1 hour, stirring every 20 minutes, until smooth.
Serve hot with chips.
recipes.healthier: Skip the meat, use half the cheese and add black beans. Serve with sliced peppers instead of chips.

recipes.title: Steak fajitas
recipes.blurb: Sizzling skirt steak, charred peppers, warm tortillas.
steps: Toss steak with half the oil, seasoning and lime. Rest 20 minutes.
Select Grill HI with Woodfire flavor and preheat until it says Add Food.
Grill steak 4 minutes per side. Rest while you cook the veg.
Grill peppers and onion in a grill basket 8–10 minutes, tossing once.
Slice the steak thinly across the grain and pile into tortillas.
recipes.healthier: Use lettuce cups or corn tortillas and load up on peppers.

recipes.title: Grilled pork chops
recipes.blurb: Thick, juicy chops with a brown sugar crust.
steps: Mix the sugar and spices. Rub the chops with oil, then the spice mix.
Select Grill HI with Woodfire flavor and preheat.
Grill 5–6 minutes per side until 145°F inside.
Rest 5 minutes.
recipes.healthier: Skip the sugar and serve with grilled apples and greens.

recipes.title: Grilled fish tacos
recipes.blurb: Flaky white fish, crunchy slaw, lime crema.
ing: ¼ cup sour cream + juice of 1 lime
steps: Brush fish with oil and season.
Select Grill MED and preheat. Grill fish 3–4 minutes per side until it flakes.
Mix sour cream with lime juice.
Fill tortillas with fish, cabbage and lime crema.
recipes.healthier: Use Greek yogurt in the crema and corn tortillas.

recipes.title: Bacon jalapeño poppers
recipes.blurb: Creamy, spicy, smoky. Gone in minutes.
steps: Mix cream cheese and cheddar. Fill each jalapeño half.
Wrap each with a half slice of bacon.
Select Air Crisp at 375°F with Woodfire flavor and preheat.
Cook 12–15 minutes until the bacon is crisp.
recipes.healthier: Use light cream cheese and turkey bacon, or skip the bacon and top with breadcrumbs.

recipes.title: BBQ chicken drumsticks
recipes.blurb: Crispy outside, sticky sauce, kid-approved.
steps: Toss drumsticks with oil and rub.
Select Air Crisp at 390°F with Woodfire flavor and preheat.
Cook 25 minutes, turning halfway.
Brush with sauce and cook 3–5 minutes more until 175°F inside.
recipes.healthier: Pull the skin off before cooking and use a no-sugar-added sauce.

recipes.title: Smoky BBQ meatloaf
recipes.blurb: Classic meatloaf with a smoky glaze. Comfort on a weeknight.
steps: Mix beef, egg, breadcrumbs, onion and salt. Shape a loaf in a foil pan.
Select Bake at 350°F with Woodfire flavor and preheat.
Bake 45 minutes. Brush with BBQ sauce and bake 15 minutes more until 160°F.
Rest 10 minutes before slicing.
recipes.healthier: Use half lean ground turkey and add grated zucchini to the mix.

recipes.title: Keto smoked chicken thighs, sugar-free glaze
recipes.blurb: Smoky, sticky thighs with no sugar in the rub or the sauce. Nothing burns black.
steps: Toss the chicken with oil, paprika, garlic powder, salt and pepper.
Fill the pellet scoop, select Smoker at 250°F and preheat.
Smoke 45 minutes.
Switch to Grill HI, brush with sugar-free BBQ sauce and grill 2–3 minutes a side until 175°F inside.

fix.q: BBQ rubs and sauces scorch on the grill.
fix.a: Sugar burns at about 350°F. A sugar-free rub and sauce let you finish over high heat for char without black, bitter spots.

key.why: All the sticky glaze, about 1 g of sugar a serving.

recipes.healthier: Already lean and low-sugar. Serve with grilled veg instead of buns.

recipes.title: Double-smoke reverse-sear steak
recipes.blurb: Smoke first at low heat, sear last. The fix for a steak that barely tastes of smoke.
ing: 2 thick ribeye or strip steaks (1½ inch)
steps: Salt the steaks and leave them uncovered in the fridge for 1 hour, or overnight.
Fill the pellet scoop with hickory. Smoker at 250°F, preheat, then smoke 25 minutes.
Add a second half-scoop of pellets and smoke until 115°F inside (about 15 more minutes).
Take the steaks out. Switch to Grill HI and preheat until Add Food.
Sear 2 minutes a side with the butter on top, to 130°F for medium-rare. Rest 5 minutes.

fix.q: Not enough smoke flavor from the Woodfire.
fix.a: Smoke sticks to cold, dry meat and stops once the surface heats up. Start cold and dry, use a stronger wood like hickory, refill the scoop once, and sear only at the end.

key.why: Hickory and mesquite taste much smokier than the default blend.

recipes.healthier: Use sirloin and skip the butter.

recipes.title: Chicken souvlaki skewers with tzatziki
recipes.blurb: Lemon-oregano chicken with a yogurt sauce. About 40 g protein a plate.
ing: 1 cup Greek yogurt + ½ grated cucumber + dill for tzatziki
steps: Marinate the chicken in oil, lemon, oregano, garlic and salt for 30 minutes (up to 8 hours).
Thread onto flat skewers, pieces touching but not squashed.
Select Grill HI and preheat until Add Food.
Grill 10–12 minutes, turning every 3, until 165°F.
Squeeze the cucumber dry and stir into the yogurt with dill and salt.

fix.q: Food spins on the skewer when you flip it.
fix.a: Round skewers act like an axle. Flat blades grip each piece, so the whole skewer turns in one go.

key.why: Flat, reusable and nothing spins. Check the length fits the grate.

recipes.healthier: Already lean. Use 0% yogurt for the tzatziki.

recipes.title: Smoked cauliflower steaks with tahini
recipes.blurb: Thick cauliflower slices, smoked then charred. A vegan main, not a side.
ing: 3 tbsp tahini + lemon + water for the drizzle
steps: Trim the leaves and cut the cauliflower into 2 thick slices through the core. Keep the loose florets.
Brush everything with oil and the spices.
Smoker at 250°F with pellets, 30 minutes. Put the florets in the grill basket so they don't fall through.
Switch to Grill HI and char 4 minutes a side until tender.
Thin the tahini with lemon and water and drizzle.

fix.q: Veggies dry out or fall through the grate.
fix.a: Smoke them low first with plenty of oil so they cook through, then char fast. Small pieces go in a basket.

key.why: Keeps florets, mushrooms and fish out of the fire.

recipes.healthier: Already a top pick.

notes: The glaze is only warmed briefly, so most of the alcohol stays in. For kids, use apple juice and vanilla instead of bourbon.
recipes.title: Bourbon-glazed smoked peaches (21+)
recipes.blurb: Smoky peach halves in a bourbon-butter glaze. Serve warm over vanilla ice cream.
steps: Melt the butter, sugar, bourbon, cinnamon and salt together for 1 minute. Off the heat.
Grill HI with Woodfire flavor, preheat until Add Food.
Grill the peaches cut side down 4 minutes, flip and spoon glaze into each.
Grill 3 more minutes. Serve with ice cream and the leftover glaze.

fix.q: Grilled fruit turns to mush or sticks.
fix.a: Use ripe-but-firm peaches, oil the grate, and don't move them for the first 4 minutes. They release on their own.

key.why: Cherry or apple pellets taste best with fruit.

recipes.healthier: Skip the sugar and serve with Greek yogurt.
